props.title: The Sleeping Car Murder
props.initialSlug: A deadly secret on the rails.

sections.content: Costa-Gavras burst onto the international film scene with this taut French thriller **The Sleeping Car Murder** (1965), bringing noir sensibilities to the European police procedural. The film showcases early glimpses of the political edge that would define his later works like **Z** (1969) and **State of Siege** (1972). With Yves Montand and Simone Signoret leading a stellar cast, the murder mystery unfolds with clockwork precision aboard the Paris-Marseille overnight train, establishing Costa-Gavras's masterful ability to build tension in confined spaces.

sections.content: The film's train setting places it in conversation with other classic railway thrillers like **Strangers on a Train** (1951) and **Murder on the Orient Express** (1974). Costa-Gavras uses the claustrophobic sleeping car compartments to ratchet up suspense, while the procedural elements draw from French crime films like **Rififi** (1955) and **Le Samouraï** (1967). The methodical police investigation, led by Inspector Grazzi, showcases the influence of Georges Simenon's Maigret novels on French crime cinema.

Beyond its thriller elements, **The Sleeping Car Murder** demonstrates Costa-Gavras's early interest in social commentary. The train's cross-section of French society - from working class to wealthy passengers - allows for subtle critique of class divisions, a theme he would explore more explicitly in later works like **Section spéciale** (1975). The film's technical precision, particularly in its use of confined spaces and parallel editing, influenced later European thrillers. SUBHEAD: Evolution of the European Police Procedural

sections.content: Costa-Gavras's approach to the procedural genre influenced a wave of European crime films that balanced entertainment with social commentary. This fusion would later be seen in works like **The Day of the Jackal** (1973) and **Investigation of a Citizen Above Suspicion** (1970), where the mechanics of police work serve as a lens for examining broader societal issues.
